title: fetch.py text unpacks MSI, CAB, WIM and similar archives through a table of extractor commands run in the map sandbox, an internal root may add rows, and 7z installs like WezTerm
goal: A table maps a file extension to an argv command and an output directory under _cache/ or _private/. fetch.py text URL runs the matching command in the sandbox kbingest map uses (allow-list environment, timeout, offline, no program or path inside the clone), reads the extracted files as it reads zip members (caps, printable strings for binaries, cut markers) and removes the directory. An internal root may add rows in its own _extractors.csv, its program on PATH outside every clone, and each run prints the program it started. The shipped table names 7z for MSI, CAB and WIM; 7z is an optional dependency installed the way WezTerm is: _tools/install_7z.py --plan, --declined and --yes [--from FILE] with each OS's pinned release URL and SHA-256 and a per-user target, PATH and profiles untouched, and /kb-setup asks before it installs. Without a matching row, or when the program is not installed, text exits 2 naming the extension, the program and the installer; an OLE compound file with no row exits 2 too; zip, tar, gzip and spreadsheet routes are unchanged. Synthetic archives only in the fixtures.

run:
import os, sys
t = '_tools/fetch_extractors.csv'
os.path.exists(t) or sys.exit('no shipped extractor table ' + t)
rows = [ln.lower() for ln in open(t, encoding='utf-8')]
miss = [e for e in ('.msi', '.cab', '.wim') if not any(e in r and '7z' in r for r in rows)]
miss and sys.exit('no 7z row for %s' % miss)

import re, subprocess, sys
r = subprocess.run([sys.executable, '_tools/install_7z.py', '--plan'], capture_output=True, text=True)
out = r.stdout
r.returncode == 0 or sys.exit('install_7z.py --plan exited %s: %s' % (r.returncode, (r.stderr or out).strip()[-200:]))
('https://' in out and re.search(r'\b[0-9a-f]{64}\b', out)) or sys.exit('the plan names no pinned https url and sha256: ' + out[:300])

import http.server, os, subprocess, sys, threading, zipfile, io, gzip
BODIES = {
    '/a.cab': (b'MSCF\0\0\0\0' + bytes(range(1, 200)), 'application/vnd.ms-cab-compressed'),
    '/a.wim': (b'MSWIM\0\0\0' + bytes(range(1, 200)), 'application/octet-stream'),
    '/a.msi': (b'\xd0\xcf\x11\xe0\xa1\xb1\x1a\xe1' + bytes(range(1, 200)), 'application/x-msi'),
}
buf = io.BytesIO()
with zipfile.ZipFile(buf, 'w') as z:
    z.writestr('note.txt', 'zip member text')
BODIES['/a.zip'] = (buf.getvalue(), 'application/zip')
BODIES['/a.txt.gz'] = (gzip.compress(b'gzip body text'), 'application/gzip')
class H(http.server.BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    def do_GET(self):
        b = BODIES.get(self.path)
        if b is None:
            self.send_response(404); self.end_headers(); return
        self.send_response(200); self.send_header('Content-Type', b[1]); self.send_header('Content-Length', str(len(b[0]))); self.end_headers(); self.wfile.write(b[0])
    def log_message(self, *a): pass
s = http.server.HTTPServer(('127.0.0.1', 0), H)
threading.Thread(target=s.serve_forever, daemon=True).start()
def text(path):
    env = {'PATH': os.path.dirname(sys.executable), 'HOME': '/nonexistent'}
    r = subprocess.run([sys.executable, '_tools/fetch.py', 'text', 'http://127.0.0.1:%d%s' % (s.server_address[1], path)], capture_output=True, text=True, env=env)
    return r.returncode, r.stdout, r.stderr

bad = []
for p in ('/a.cab', '/a.wim'):
    rc, out, err = text(p)
    ok = rc == 2 and p[-3:] in err and '7z' in err and 'install_7z' in err
    ok or bad.append('%s: exit %s, %r' % (p, rc, err[:160]))
bad and sys.exit('with 7z absent text must exit 2 naming the extension, 7z and the installer: ' + '; '.join(bad))

gates.question: Where do the sandbox helpers (scrub_env, NETWORK_OFF, tool_exe, run_tool, kill_tree) live so fetch.py and kbingest.py share them?
options: A new module kbsandbox.py that both import, moved out of kbingest.py without a change of behaviour
Copy the few helpers into fetch.py
gates.recommendation: A new module kbsandbox.py that both import, moved out of kbingest.py without a change of behaviour
gates.reason: because one sandbox with one test is safer than two, and fetch.py should not load a 2300-line module to unpack a file
gates.answer: A new module kbsandbox.py that both import, moved out of kbingest.py without a change of behaviour

gates.question: Which extractor programs does the shipped table name for MSI, CAB and WIM, and what does it do when none is installed?
options: One cross-platform program (7z) for all three, and text exits 2 naming 7z when it is absent
The platform's own tools (expand.exe, DISM, msiexec) on Windows and 7z elsewhere
gates.recommendation: One cross-platform program (7z) for all three, and text exits 2 naming 7z when it is absent
gates.reason: because msiexec and DISM can run installer logic or need administrator rights, while 7z only lists and extracts
gates.answer: 7z for MSI, CAB and WIM; 7z is an optional dependency installed the way WezTerm is: a pinned per-user installer (_tools/install_7z.py --plan | --declined | --yes [--from FILE], each OS's release URL and SHA-256 pin, a per-user target, PATH and profiles untouched, /kb-setup asks first); text exits 2 naming 7z and the installer when 7z is absent

gates.question: Which roots may add rows in _extractors.csv, given a row names a program this machine will run on a downloaded file?
options: Internal roots only; the program must be found on PATH outside every clone; each run prints the program it started
No root: the table in the repository is the only one
gates.recommendation: Internal roots only; the program must be found on PATH outside every clone; each run prints the program it started
gates.reason: because a team trusts its own root's rows, while a public or fetched root would let its content choose what runs on every machine that serves it
gates.answer: Internal roots only; the program must be found on PATH outside every clone; each run prints the program it started

notes:
Premise (plan time, synthetic bodies): read_text returns None for a CAB (MSCF) or WIM (MSWIM) body, so text exits 2; an MSI body (OLE header d0cf11e0) is worse: the raw bytes come back as replacement-character text and text exits 0. A zip-based MSIX already reads through the zip route, as should a zip-based .intunewin outer container (from memory): no new rows for them. fetch.py reads zip and tar members in memory only; the new route writes untrusted contents to disk, so it needs caps on bytes, file count and depth, refusal of absolute and parent paths and of links, and removal of the directory in a finally. kbingest.py already has scrub_env, NETWORK_OFF, tool_exe, run_tool and kill_tree; fetch.py has none, so they move to kbsandbox.py (g1).
Operator: g2 internal roots only; g3 7z, installed like WezTerm. Order: after the kbingest.py story; shares kb/_self/tools.md with S2 and S3.
Checks 1, 2, 3 and 9 pass before the work and pin behaviour that must stay unchanged (the existing fetch routes, the sandbox guards, the test ids); every other check fails before it with a one-line reason.
Checks 7 to 9 serve synthetic bodies from a local HTTP server and run fetch.py text with a PATH holding only the Python directory, so 7z is absent whatever the host has. Check 0 is the guard test the worker writes: table lookup, scrubbed environment and timeout, caps and traversal refusal, directory removal, internal-roots-only rule, the printed program name.
